title: Field extension over a separably closed base induces a component bijection
statement: Let $k$ be a separably closed field [def-pc-separably-closed], let $L/k$ be any field extension [def-pc-field-extension], and let $Z$ be any scheme over $k$ [def-weil-scheme-over-base]. Put $Z_L=Z\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}L$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. A connected component means a maximal nonempty connected subset of the underlying topological space [def-weil-connected-scheme]. The projection $p:Z_L\to Z$ induces a bijection from the set of connected components of $Z_L$ to the set of connected components of $Z$, sending each component to the unique component containing its image. No finiteness hypothesis on $Z$ or $L/k$ is imposed.

proof.text: Put $W=\operatorname{Spec}L$, with structure morphism induced by the field extension $k\to L$ [def-pc-field-extension]. By [def-weil-affine-spectrum] its underlying space has exactly one point. This space is nonempty, and two disjoint nonempty subsets cannot exist in a singleton. Hence it has no decomposition into two nonempty clopen subsets and is connected by [def-weil-connected-scheme]. This requires only that $L$ is a field, not that $L/k$ is finite or algebraic.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-separably-closed-geometrically-connected] to the connected $k$-scheme $W$ of step 1. Its hypotheses are exactly that $k$ is separably closed and that $W$ is a scheme over $k$ and connected. It follows that $W$ is geometrically connected over $k$. This supplies the geometric-connectedness input of the proof of Tag 0363 without a new tensor-product lemma; the reused node has an independently finished project proof.

source.place: Tag 0363, label lemma-separably-closed-field-connected-components, proof; Tag 0385, label lemma-bijection-connected-components

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-geometrically-connected-product-components] with its $X=W$ and $Y=Z$. Step 2 supplies the only extra hypothesis. Thus $q:W\times_k Z\to Z$ induces the stated bijection. By [def-pc-fibre-product], swapping the two projections gives mutually inverse morphisms $Z\times_kW\rightleftarrows W\times_k Z$: their composites have the original projections, so uniqueness in the universal property makes both composites identities. The swap commutes with the projections to $Z$, identifying $q$ with $p$. Write $h$ for the underlying swap homeomorphism. If $C$ is a component, then $h(C)$ is nonempty and connected by continuity. If a nonempty connected subset $D$ contains $h(C)$, continuity of $h^{-1}$ makes $h^{-1}(D)$ connected and containing $C$; maximality gives $h^{-1}(D)=C$, hence $D=h(C)$. Thus $h$ sends components to components, and applying this argument to $h^{-1}$ gives the inverse component bijection. Therefore the bijection for $q$ is precisely the component map induced by $p$. When $Z$ is empty both fibre products are empty and the bijection is the unique map between empty component sets; otherwise the argument uses no finiteness of either component set.
